failure_reason: The hot_update workload did not create sustained row-level lock contention on a single hot record, so Innodb_row_lock_waits did not increase. As a result, no slow queries were generated (lock waits did not exceed the slow query threshold), and the background QPS did not drop. Likely causes: (1) updates were spread across many keys or committed too quickly (autocommit-like behavior) without an explicit lock hold, (2) concurrency and hold time were too low to create measurable waits, and/or (3) the TPCC workload was not focused on the same hot row/warehouse, making collisions rare. If your current set of injected_nodes does not include a background TPCC load or a way to concentrate terminals on the same warehouse/district, you will need to add such injected_nodes for the chain to propagate.
suggested_changes: Pin hot_update to a single hot row to guarantee contention: target the TPC-C district primary key (d_w_id=1, d_id=1).
Use an explicit lock-holding transaction in hot_update so other workers are forced to wait: BEGIN; SELECT ... FOR UPDATE; sleep for 3–5 seconds; UPDATE; COMMIT.
Increase hot_update concurrency to >= 64 workers, with zero think time and a high request rate (>= 800 ops/s) to generate a backlog waiting on the held lock.
Run the hot_update action for at least 180–300 seconds to ensure Innodb_row_lock_waits and slow query counters have time to move and be sampled.

Ensure the TPCC workload is active and focuses on the same hotspot (e.g., warehouse_id=1, district_id=1) with enough terminals (>= 64). If your current injected_nodes do not include a TPCC load node or cannot skew warehouse selection, you will need to add such an injected node.
Align with slow query detection: if long_query_time is 1s, hold the lock for >= 3s so blocked statements are logged; otherwise lower long_query_time to <= 1s or extend the hold time further.
Verify the workload is hitting the primary/writer instance (not a replica) and that the isolation level is at least REPEATABLE READ so row locks are effective.
Start with a brief warm-up (e.g., 30–60s) before injection to establish a baseline, then inject hot_update to clearly observe the ratio increases and QPS drop.

transaction_script_steps: SELECT d_ytd FROM district WHERE d_w_id=1 AND d_id=1 FOR UPDATE
UPDATE district SET d_ytd = d_ytd + 1 WHERE d_w_id=1 AND d_id=1

risk_warning: This adjustment intentionally creates heavy lock contention on a TPC-C hotspot and will block New-Order/Payment transactions that touch the same district row. Expect significant QPS drops, possible deadlocks, and long transaction waits. Undo logs may grow during the hold; ensure adequate disk space and run in a non-production environment. Updating d_ytd changes financial counters; restore from snapshot or discard data after testing.
